doc.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: The album Moody Plays Mancini
summary: They discuss the soprano sound on the Mancini album and how the label's concept came about.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Right. I wanted to talk for a moment about one of your recent albums, “Moody Plays Mancini,” which is — your soprano sound came off just gorgeous on that record.
And in fact I just wanted to see if I got this up here—
Well it’s a gorgeous sound. How did this album come about?
Well the company wanted a concept. And that’s the thing nowadays, concept.
So we came up with the concept. Frank Sinatra before this. And then after this, Mancini, so that was the concept. But that’s how that came about. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
